items.headline: Police say Jantar Mantar unfit as protest site
items.text: Delhi Police told the Supreme Court on Tuesday that Jantar Mantar, a public road holding about 1,500 people, should never have been a protest site; petitioners say de-notifying it violates free assembly.

photo.alt: A tall red and beige stone instrument with arched openings, on a lawn.
photo.caption: The Jantar Mantar observatory in New Delhi. The road beside it was the capital's main protest site until police de-notified it on 11 October.

items.headline: High Court takes up killings of Karnataka lawyers
items.text: Karnataka's High Court opened a PIL on Tuesday over violence against lawyers, including two October murders, asking the state how it handles lawyers' complaints against police; no state response was reported.

photo.alt: A large red colonnaded building with a triangular pediment behind a fence and gardens.
photo.caption: The High Court of Karnataka in Bengaluru (Attara Kacheri), in 2019.

items.headline: Guwahati shooting accused killed in police custody
items.text: Ghanakanta Gogoi, accused in the 26 October Guwahati hotel shooting that killed five, died when police fired during his transfer in Sivasagar; police say he tried to seize an officer's pistol. No inquiry was reported.

photo.alt: A tall dark stone temple on a lawn with clipped bushes, framed by trees.
photo.caption: A temple beside the Na-Pukhuri tank in Sivasagar, Assam, in 2026.

items.headline: Court: encrypted app no ground for PSA detention
items.text: The J&K High Court quashed the Public Safety Act detention of a Pulwama man held since July 2025 over alleged militant contacts, saying use of an encrypted app was no adequate basis for detention.

photo.alt: A narrow alley between tall brick houses with wooden windows and tangled wires overhead; a woman in a headscarf stands in the shade.
photo.caption: An alley in Srinagar's old city in 2016. The Public Safety Act is the main preventive detention law in Jammu and Kashmir.

items.headline: Bihar police officer fires on villagers, one dead
items.text: A police ASI fired his service pistol at villagers in Madhubani district early Tuesday, killing one and injuring three, police say; he has been suspended, faces a murder case and is absconding.

photo.alt: A railway platform whose walls are covered in colourful Mithila paintings, with red chairs and a few people.
photo.caption: Madhubani railway station, Bihar, decorated with Mithila paintings, in 2021.

items.headline: 61 alleged undocumented migrants detained in Ahmedabad
items.text: Police detained 61 people, including women and children, in Ahmedabad on Monday as alleged undocumented immigrants, mostly Bangladeshi, they say; officials say deportation proceedings are under way.

photo.alt: The carved wooden facade of an old two-storey house with balconies and pillars.
photo.caption: A carved house front in Ahmedabad's old city, in 2023.

items.place: Wadi Majrur, Al-Malha locality, North Darfur, Sudan
items.headline: Drone kills two travellers in North Darfur
items.text: A drone struck a vehicle in Wadi Majrur, Al-Malha locality, on Sunday, killing two civilians, a local rights monitor told Radio Tamazuj; it blames the army, and no army response was reported.

photo.alt: Rows of low houses and walled compounds on sandy ground, seen from the air.
photo.caption: El Fasher, capital of North Darfur, seen from the air in 2010. Al-Malha locality lies to its north.
photo.credit: Fraktion DIE LINKE. im Bundestag / Wikimedia Commons

items.headline: Bombs hit Ukrainian aid centre, 33 dead
items.text: At least 33 people died when aerial bombs hit an aid distribution centre in Komyshuvakha, Zaporizhzhia, on Monday, Ukrainian officials say; Russia's defence ministry says it targeted military units.

photo.alt: A single-storey public building with a red roof and flags, behind a fence and a road.
photo.caption: The public services centre in Komyshuvakha, Zaporizhzhia region, in 2025.

items.place: Gaza City and Khan Younis, Gaza
items.headline: Girl killed in drone strike on Gaza tent
items.text: Three Palestinians, including a girl hit when a drone struck a tent in Gaza City, were killed on Tuesday, medical sources told Anadolu; no Israeli military comment was reported.

photo.alt: A dirt road between collapsed and badly damaged multi-storey buildings and piles of rubble.
photo.caption: Destroyed buildings in the Sheikh Radwan district of Gaza City, February 2025.

items.place: International Court of Justice, The Hague · Rakhine State, Myanmar
items.headline: World Court to rule in Myanmar genocide case
items.text: The International Court of Justice will rule on 19 November in Gambia's case accusing Myanmar of genocide against the Rohingya, over 700,000 of whom fled in 2017, HRW said; no Myanmar comment was reported.

photo.alt: Old stone temples and stupas among green trees and grass, with a few people and cows on a dirt path, under grey clouds.
photo.caption: Temples at Mrauk-U, Rakhine State, in 2017. The Rohingya were driven from northern Rakhine in 2017.

items.headline: Ethiopia suspends one of its oldest newspapers
items.text: Ethiopia's Media Authority indefinitely suspended the Reporter, the last private Amharic newspaper, on 2 November, accusing it of content against "national interests"; HRW calls it part of a wider media crackdown.

photo.alt: A city street with men standing around a table football game, parked cars and tall buildings behind.
photo.caption: Cunningham Street in Addis Ababa, in 2023.

items.headline: Two Uyghurs face deportation from Thailand, HRW warns
items.text: Two Uyghur men held in Thailand since 2014 were moved to Bangkok immigration detention ahead of possible return to China, HRW said on Tuesday; Thai officials told MPs China had demanded their return.

photo.alt: A city street corner with shops, cafes, a food cart and dense overhead cables.
photo.caption: Suan Phlu Road in Bangkok, in 2026. The two men are held at the immigration detention centre in Suan Phlu.

focus.title: Preventive detention in Jammu & Kashmir: what the courts are finding
focus.dek: J&K's High Court keeps quashing Public Safety Act detentions over vague police reports; on 30 October it ruled an encrypted app no ground to detain. The administration cites "established peace".
focus.alt: A narrow alley between tall brick houses with wooden windows and tangled wires overhead; a woman in a headscarf stands in the shade.
